lines.t: Hello! Welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
Hi! I'm Sam. Today we talk about the future.
Sam, you have a new thing. What is it?
It is a robot! I bought it yesterday. Soon, very soon, it will do all my work.
Wow. What can it do?
Tomorrow it will make tea. Next week it will make dinner. Next year it will clean the house.
Go on. And today?
Today it can say "hello." And it can turn on the light.
That is not much. Only two things.
Wait. Robot, turn off the light. Robot, make tea.
And?
It turns off the light. Then it turns on the music. Very loud, not quiet.
[laugh] And the tea?
Maybe later. My phone says the robot needs a new computer. In the morning it will wake me up. That is the plan. I am going to sleep now.
[laugh] See you tomorrow!

words.en: what lets you see; a lamp
stop sleeping; make someone stop sleeping

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is the future. Leyla, what will the world look like in fifty years?
I think technology will change everything. We will probably work from home. On the moon.
[laugh] Maybe! I think we'll have flying cars. I'll take off from my balcony.
Sam, you can't even park a normal car.
True. I haven't worked out a plan. But look, this morning my phone said, "Forecast: sunny all day."
And?
It rained. I had no umbrella, and I left the window open. My robot vacuum cleaner carried on cleaning, and when I came home, my kitchen was a lake.
[laugh] And the robot?
It just carried on cleaning the lake. I think it was proud.
The future will be like that: clever machines and people who forget the window.
I think it will get better. In ten years, a robot will cook for us.
We'll see. Who knows? Maybe your robot will turn into a swimming teacher.
Rude. But possible. See you next time!

words.en: machines and computers made with science
a machine that does work by itself
a thing with parts that does work
what you decide to do and how
find the answer or a plan by thinking

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is the future, and the people who try to predict it.
My grandmother is eighty. Two years ago she said, "Video calls are a stupid invention." Last night she called me twelve times.
That's an amazing development.
It turned out her thumb was the problem. The screen goes dark when she covers the camera. She did not expect that.
[laugh] A good prediction: everyone finds a technology they love, eventually.
My trend prediction: in five years everybody will have a robot, and nobody will know how to use it.
Our generation will make it normal, and the next generation will come up with something we can't imagine.
I read that the next big advance will be talking to computers like people. Only time will tell.
My dad says it's a matter of time before a robot dances salsa.
Will it beat your dad?
In the long run, yes. But for now he wins, and he still cheats at the end — he stops counting at three.
Hmm. What do you think will go on forever, whatever changes?
Grandmothers. And cards.
A question for our listeners: what do you expect in ten years, and what do you hope will never change?
Mine are the same two. See you next time!

words.en: a new thing someone makes for the first time
in the end, after a long time
a general change in what people do
people born around the same time
be found to be true in the end
it will surely happen, but not yet
